objective: Characterize exactly when identifying the two neighbors of a degree-two vertex preserves the triangle-free planar subcubic class, and derive a conditional reducibility consequence of the Z20 extension criterion.

atomic_claims.text: For a degree-two v with neighbors u,w, the simple quotient identifying u,w after deleting v stays in the contract class exactly when their external-neighborhood union has size at most three and v lies on no five-cycle.
Every (20,7)-coloring of that quotient lifts to equal neighbor colors in G-v and has seven extensions at v; hence a vertex-minimal obstruction cannot contain a class-preserving such reduction.
Every degree-two vertex in a vertex-minimal obstruction lies on a five-cycle or has two degree-three neighbors with disjoint external neighborhoods.

assumptions: Finite simple triangle-free planar G of maximum degree at most three; v has exactly two distinct neighbors.
Parallel edges in the identified quotient are suppressed; loops do not arise because the two neighbors are nonadjacent.
Planarity under edge contraction and the generated local extension candidate c01 are explicit premises.
Minimal-counterexample consequences are conditional on minimum vertex order in the contract class.
risks: The local quotient criterion is not a whole-problem proof.
Removing the five-cycle condition or the degree-union condition makes class preservation fail, as shown by explicit small witnesses.
Prior candidate transport is not mathematical verification.
No graph enumeration, solver, kernel execution, or verifier receipt is claimed.
